title: Token-provenance ledger for streaming responses with mixed KV/prefix cache hits and microbatch aggregation
creator: Ava Morales
description: Problem statement: Streaming responses commonly mix tokens emitted from a cache (prefix or KV hits) and tokens generated by the model. Current metering attributes tokens at microbatch level and then prorates when batches are coalesced, but we lack a deterministic, per-request ledger that preserves token provenance for streaming sessions. This causes three classes of billing/accounting correctness issues: 1) under/over-charging when a stream starts with cached tokens and then switches to generated tokens within the same microbatch; 2) quota and rate-limit enforcement errors when provisional capacity is used for speculative warmups or prefetched tokens are later evicted mid-stream; 3) reconciliation problems for partial streams (client disconnects or resumed sessions) across billing windows. The goal is to introduce a lightweight per-request token-provenance ledger that records token segments with provenance tags and microbatch associations, enabling correct billing, quota adjustments, and deterministic reconciliation for streaming and partial-response use cases.
acceptance_criteria: Create an in-memory token-provenance ledger attached to the request context that records segments: {provenance_tag, token_count, model_variant, microbatch_id, estimate_cost_weight}
Ledger events emitted to the billing-event stream at microbatch emission and on finalization, enabling offline aggregation that matches chargeback with <=0.1% variance in simulation tests
Rate-limit windows and quota checks only count generated tokens immediately; prefetched/cached tokens are accounted but do not decrement live quota until finalization policy confirms ownership

Partial-stream cases (client disconnect) trigger an immediate ledger flush and reconciliation job that produces an audit entry and a proposed charge; at least 95% of simulated disconnect scenarios reconcile within 30s

End-to-end integration tests for: full cache-hit stream, partial cache-hit then generated tokens, mid-request eviction, speculative prefetch becoming real request, and microbatch coalescing across tenants.
design_decision_log: Decision 2026-02-22: Use provenance tags: 'cached_prefix', 'kv_hit', 'speculative_warmup', 'generated' to keep attribution simple and extensible.
Decision 2026-02-25: Ledger kept in request-local memory with bounded size (tokens segments compacted by run-length) and persisted as compact events to Kafka for billing reconciliation.

Decision 2026-03-01: Billing will bill at emission-time for 'generated' tokens to preserve realtime revenue signals; cached tokens will be recorded and billed in a reconciliation pass to allow tenant-level credits in edge cases.

Decision 2026-03-04: For coalesced microbatches, microbatch-level cost_weight is prorated by token provenance when producing billing events; the offline aggregator will apply a stable-sort by microbatch_id to ensure deterministic splits.
implementation_notes: Add TokenLedger object to request context with APIs: append_segment(provenance, count, variant, microbatch_id, estimate_weight), flush_partial(reason), finalize_and_emit()

Modify serving runtime to call append_segment when emitting cached tokens (both prefix and KV) and when generating tokens. For speculative warmups, mark segments as speculative_warmup and include correlation_id to originating request if present.
On microbatch coalescing code path, attach microbatch_id and per-tenant slice ids to ledger segments before emission so billing events can be attributed after aggregation.
Billing-event schema changes: add fields provenance_tag and microbatch_id and ensure events are idempotent via request_id + segment_index key.

Introduce a short-lived reservation for quota checks when speculative_warmup occurs: reservation expires after 5s unless converted to 'generated' or released. Reservations do not decrement long-term quota until finalized.
test_plan: Unit tests for TokenLedger: segment compaction, idempotent emits, bounding memory usage
Integration harness that simulates 10k streaming sessions with a mix of cache-hit ratios (0%, 30%, 70%, 100%) — verify billed token counts match expected within 0.1%
Chaos tests: mid-stream KV eviction, client disconnects, resumed sessions across billing windows — verify reconciliation jobs produce audit records and suggested credits/refunds
Load test: ensure ledger overhead adds <2% p99 latency on path for typical 32-token prefix cache hits
Canary: route 2% of production traffic to a branch with ledger enabled and compare billing totals and quotas against control group for 24h.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement ledger + event emitter, enable for internal tenants and 2% external traffic, monitor billing pipeline and p99 latency. Rollout window: 48h.
Phase 2 (validation): Run reconciliation job nightly for canary traffic and compare charges to legacy pipeline. Fix deterministic edge cases. Window: 1 week.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Increase to 25% then 100% over two weeks contingent on reconciliation parity and rate-limit behavior.
Rollback: Feature flag to disable ledger emission; revert runtime hooks if false positives in rate-limiting observed.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Ava Morales: Initial writeup. Noted that many prior tickets assume microbatch-level attribution; this ticket creates a per-request primitive to make future meters simpler.
2026-02-24 - Lydia Chen (PM): Please ensure UX team is comfortable with any customer-visible billing changes; we'll need billing FAQ and predictable behavior for partner customers.
2026-03-02 - Ravi Singh: Implementation branch created. Implemented append_segment and in-memory compaction. Still integrating microbatch_id plumbing with serving runtime.
2026-03-05 - R&D (ops): Observed low-volume outliers where speculative_warmup segments were double-counted in the offline aggregator; added idempotency keys to events to fix.

2026-03-09 - Finance: Prefer emitting preliminary charge estimates to billing pipeline with reconciliation marks to avoid sudden customer-facing charge spikes; agreed approach documented in Confluence.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Singh: Swapped reservation expiry from 2s -> 5s after seeing transient prefetch conversions in canary; updated tests and canary config.
